question: Evaluate $$\sin^{-1}\left(\sin\frac{7\pi}{4}\right)+\cos^{-1}\left(\cos\frac{5\pi}{3}\right).$$
explanation:
Principal value of the inverse sine term
The principal value range of $\sin^{-1}x$ is $\left[-\frac{\pi}{2},\frac{\pi}{2}\right]$. Since $$\sin\frac{7\pi}{4}=-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}=\sin\left(-\frac{\pi}{4}\right),$$ we obtain $$\sin^{-1}\left(\sin\frac{7\pi}{4}\right)=-\frac{\pi}{4}.$$

Principal value of the inverse cosine term
The principal value range of $\cos^{-1}x$ is $[0,\pi]$. Also, $$\cos\frac{5\pi}{3}=\frac{1}{2}=\cos\frac{\pi}{3}.$$ Therefore, $$\cos^{-1}\left(\cos\frac{5\pi}{3}\right)=\frac{\pi}{3}.$$

Addition of principal values
Thus, the required value is $$-\frac{\pi}{4}+\frac{\pi}{3}=\frac{-3\pi+4\pi}{12}=\frac{\pi}{12}.$$
